metadata.description: Savannah, Florida & Western Railway (the Plant System's Georgia-Florida core) with its predecessors - Savannah, Albany & Gulf 1858-1863 and Atlantic & Gulf 1863-1879 - and the post-1902 Atlantic Coast Line continuations that no other layer draws. Savannah - Waycross - Thomasville - Bainbridge, the Waycross Short Line (1881-83 only; later years drawn in plant_system_florida.geojson), the Chattahoochee branch, DuPont - Live Oak, Live Oak - Gainesville, High Springs - Archer; ACL Savannah - Jesup - Waycross, the Folkston Cutoff, Waycross - Bainbridge, Albany - Thomasville, Thomasville - Perry, DuPont - High Springs and High Springs - Gainesville.
metadata.colour_normalization: Rule 4: Plant System colour #CA6702 pulled programmatically from plant_system_florida.geojson (plant-system-waycross-tampa) - it is the only colour any 'Plant System (...)' company carries in data/. Atlantic Coast Line colour #5B8C5A pulled from acl-waycross-tampa (same file), identical across all 'Atlantic Coast Line Railroad' features. Savannah, Albany and Gulf (#7B4F9D) and Atlantic and Gulf (#2E7D8C) are new to data/ and were checked unused by any other feature. The SA&G and A&G are treated as two companies: the SA&G was absorbed by the A&G in 1863.
metadata.ownership_splits: Split at 1 May 1863 (SA&G consolidated into the A&G; before that the SA&G ran every train, including over A&G-owned track west of Screven), Nov/Dec 1879 (Plant purchase, SF&W organized; boundary year 1879 on both sides as in other Plant features), and 1 July 1902 (ACL purchase). The 1881-84 Waycross & Florida / East Florida and the Live Oak & Rowland's Bluff / LOT&CH are Plant companies run as SF&W from opening - no split. Features of different eras share identical geometry where they cover the same track.
omitted: [15] Plant System Albany Branch (Thomasville - Albany), 1889 [ANCHOR] PROVISIONAL: rests only on Thomasville Daily Times-Enterprise search snippets (1889-05-19 p3, 1889-10-27 p3) not read on the page; the report says NONE unless confirmed. Not drawn. A&G years 1875-1879 and ACL 1928-1957 are drawn.

[19] Plant System Monticello Branch (Thomasville - Monticello 1st station), 1890 [ANCHOR] PROVISIONAL: rests only on a Times-Enterprise 1890-07-20 p3 snippet not read on the page. Not drawn. The 1888 branch north of the Perry Cutoff junction appears only in the ACL Thomasville - Perry feature (1928-1957).
[11] Folkston Cutoff, SF&W era 1901-02: drawable NONE (no passenger year confirmed). ACL era drawn from 1916.
[20] Lake City Branch: drawable NONE (no passenger year in any era; freight only in the 1952 Guide).
[31] Chattahoochee Branch, ACL era: drawable NONE (freight only by Dec 1951; no ACL passenger year confirmed).
[21] Alabama Midland Bainbridge - Montgomery (Plant 1890-1902): a pointer block, belongs in its own Alabama Midland / Plant layer; not drawn here.
[22]-[24] Brunswick & Western, Charleston & Savannah, South Florida / JT&KW: ALREADY DRAWN in their own layers.

[10] Waycross Short Line 1884-1902 and ACL Waycross - Folkston - Jacksonville 1902-1971: already drawn by plant_system_florida.geojson on the same track; this layer adds only the 1881-1883 Plant years.
ACL [26] beyond 1951 and Bainbridge - Montgomery: later years rest on an unchecked Wikipedia statement; Alabama Midland geometry not traced.

1859-60 SA&G service west of Screven, 1864 A&G service, 1866-1867/1874 A&G reopening years, 1893-96 High Springs - Archer, 1902-1915 on the Folkston Cutoff and 1902-1927 Albany - Thomasville: all withheld as unconfirmed.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN-START spans (first confirmed year, not a known start): A&G Screven - Thomasville 1868, A&G Savannah - Screven 1875, A&G Thomasville - Bainbridge 1875, A&G Albany Branch 1875, A&G DuPont - Tarver 1870, A&G Tarver - Live Oak 1875, Plant High Springs - Archer 1897, ACL Folkston Cutoff 1916. RailGa lists A&G '1870', SA&G '1859' and '1863' timetable images whose links are broken; reading them would likely move these earlier.
OPEN-END spans (last confirmed year, not a known end): ACL Jesup - Waycross 1951, ACL Waycross - Thomasville - Bainbridge 1951, ACL High Springs - Gainesville 1951.

ANCHOR spans (one proven year): SA&G-successor A&G Savannah - Thomasville 1863; A&G Screven - Thomasville 1865; Plant Chattahoochee Branch 1884 (by routing inference from the 1884 SF&W advertisement).

Thomasville Daily Times-Enterprise (Georgia Historic Newspapers, sn88054087) 1889-05-19 p3, 1889-10-27 p3 and 1890-07-20 p3 - behind a browser check on 2026-11-09; reading them would settle the Albany and Monticello branches (omitted) and widen the Chattahoochee anchor.
Folkston Cutoff: when did passenger trains move onto it after its 1901 construction? An ACL 1903-1910 timetable would settle it.
Florida Branch opening: Wikipedia DuPont-Lakeland Line says 1863; RailGa, CSA and UNF say March 1865, with the Florida rails removed again by 1866. Rebuild date not found.
Live Oak - Gainesville completion: 1884 (Wikipedia LOT&CH) vs 1883 (Wikipedia DuPont-Lakeland Line). Drawing unaffected (first confirmed year 1884).
High Springs - Archer (1893): building company not named in the sources read.
Waycross - Montgomery passenger service after 1951: Wikipedia carries it to 1979 (South Wind / Floridian); not checked against a primary source.
Brunswick & Western control: 1884 (RailGa sfw.html, Wikipedia SF&W 'bought') vs 1888 (RailGa plant.html) - recorded for brunswick_and_western_railroad.geojson, no action here.
Alabama Midland: Wikipedia Waycross-Montgomery Line says merged into the SF&W July 1890; Wikipedia SF&W / RailGa say controlling interest 1890, merger 1901.
Savannah SF&W East Broad Street depot, the 1881-83 Jacksonville terminal and the River Junction connection are not pinned on the map (see each feature's geometry_quality).
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates unless a segment note says otherwise (the 1884 five-trains-a-day and the 1865 tri-weekly figures are sourced).
known_defects_elsewhere: atlantic_coast_line.geojson florida-special-ny-miami-pre-champion (Atlantic Coast Line: Florida Special), drawn 1888-1939 on the Jesup - Nahunta - Folkston cutoff: the cutoff was built in 1901, so 1888-1900 are drawn on an alignment that did not exist (Rule 2), and 1901-~1915 are unproven on it; pre-1901 trains ran Jesup - Waycross - Folkston.

atlantic_coast_line.geojson Florida Special 1902-1939 segment is coloured #CA6702 (Plant) with a joint company string although its own note says the ACL ran it - needs a split at 1902 to ACL colour (Rule 4).
atlantic_coast_line.geojson Florida Special is drawn south of Jacksonville to Miami from 1888, but the FEC did not reach Miami until 1896.

plant_system_florida.geojson plant-system-waycross-tampa (1884-1902): Jacksonville - Sanford drawn from 1884, about two years before the JT&KW track (c.1886), and 1886-1899 in Plant colour for a road Plant did not own until its 1899 reorganization (Rule 4 - needs checking whether Plant trains ran over the JT&KW by agreement); its Waycross - Jacksonville leg is under-drawn by 1881-1883 (filled by this layer).

properties.line: Savannah, Albany and Gulf: Savannah – Screven
properties.speed_source: estimated: no source read gives a running time for this line in this era; a typical figure for a Southern single-track steam road of the period
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror) traced with opstrace.py: ways tagged old_railway_operator=ACL preferred (cost 1x), untagged rail 1.25x; Douglas-Peucker 8 m, reversals trimmed
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap end to end: 67.9 mi drawn vs 69.4 mi Savannah - Screven (Fowler ACL mileposts; the SA&G's own road was 72 mi to Little Satilla). No straight-line leg. Savannah end drawn to about 32.065 N, 81.088 W on the ex-ACL east-side track (OSM 'Savannah & Old Fort Railroad'), standing for the SA&G / A&G / SF&W depot on East Broad Street (closed 1904); the exact depot site is not pinned and the point is good to about 0.5 mi. The approach is the modern ex-ACL alignment; 19th-century realignments in Savannah have not been checked. Drawn to Screven (No. 7), not the Little Satilla bridge 2.6 mi beyond, which was the 1858 service terminus.

segments.note: The Savannah, Albany & Gulf's own 72 mi, 5 ft gauge steam road. Start 1858 = the 1858 Dinsmore guide entries (Fowler 'x') at Way's, Miller's, Fleming's, McIntosh, Walthourville, Johnson's, Doctor Town, Drawdy's and Little Satilla (then the terminus); stations had opened piecemeal from Sept 1856, but those are opening dates, not passenger proof, so 1856-57 is withheld. 28 Jan 1861 SA&G notice: passenger trains daily except Sunday, Savannah - Boston No. 18. Ends 1 May 1863 when the SA&G was consolidated into the Atlantic & Gulf (ownership change, not an end of service - continues as the A&G features). Headway: one train a day each way (1440) from the 1861 notice; earlier frequency not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 1858 Dinsmore letters (Fowler GA lines 10-11), daily service from the SA&G notice in the Savannah Morning News 28 Jan 1861 (CSA transcription), end at the 1 May 1863 consolidation (Wikipedia A&G; RailGa). Per research/branches/savannah_florida_and_western_railway.txt block [1].

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap end to end: 131.0 mi drawn vs 132 mi Screven - Thomasville (A&G annual report 1 Feb 1862; Superintendent's report 1866). No straight-line leg. Waycross is drawn through the modern CSX layout, not the 1859-80s Tebeauville/No. 9 junction. About 8.6 mi just west of Valdosta run on ways OSM tags old_railway_operator='Georgia and Florida' (the corridor the two roads share there); the mileage agrees with the documented figure, so this is taken as the A&G/SF&W line, but it is flagged.

segments.note: Atlantic & Gulf-owned track ('the Main Trunk'), but the A&G had no rolling stock: the SA&G ran every train over it until the May 1863 consolidation (A&G annual report 1 Feb 1862: 'you have no rolling stock'; the SA&G 'has continued to run their cars on your Road'), so the operator and colour here are the SA&G's. Track opened in stages - Blackshear May 1859, No. 9 July 1859, Homerville Dec 1859, DuPont Feb 1860, Valdosta July 1860, Quitman late 1860, Boston 28 Jan 1861, Thomasville 16 Apr 1861 - and very probably carried passengers as it went, but the first passenger proof read is the SA&G notice of daily trains Savannah - Boston effective 28 Jan 1861; the 1859-60 years are WITHHELD for lack of a timetable (RailGa's '1859 timetable' link is broken). Thomasville: 'cars rolling daily' over all 132 mi by 1 Feb 1862. Ends at the 1 May 1863 consolidation. Headway: daily from the 1861 notice.
sources: Segment-level: start from the SA&G notice eff. 28 Jan 1861 (Savannah Morning News, CSA transcription) and the A&G annual report of 1 Feb 1862; Thomasville opening 16 Apr 1861 from the Wikipedia A&G station table; end at the 1863 consolidation. Per research/branches/savannah_florida_and_western_railway.txt block [2].

segments.note: [ANCHOR] Only 1863 is proven: an A&G schedule effective 21 July 1863 (Southern Recorder 19 Jul 1863, via CSA) and Fowler one-off entries 'Drawdos 1863t' near Jesup and 'Groover 1863LG' (= Dixie). Service certainly ran wider than this - from the May 1863 consolidation and very probably into 1864, until Sherman's March destroyed about 40 miles of the east end (Altamaha bridge battle 19 Dec 1864, Savannah fell 21 Dec 1864) - but no other year is confirmed (a CSA 'SR 1 Sep 1864' notice was not opened). Do not widen without evidence. Headway: daily is an estimate.

segments.note: Post-war A&G main line, west of Screven. START IS [OPEN] AT THE EARLY END: 1868 is the first CONFIRMED post-war year (Fowler 'Malvern 1868G', between Blackshear and Waycross), not a known reopening date; 1875 Official Guide 'y' entries cover the whole line. RailGa lists an A&G '1870 timetable' (broken link). Do not move the start earlier without evidence. Ends Nov/Dec 1879 - Plant's purchase at foreclosure 4 Nov 1879, SF&W organized 9 Dec 1879 (ownership change; continues as the Plant System features). Headway: two trains a day each way in the Florida season per the c.1875 A&G advertisement; 720 is an estimate for the year round.
sources: Segment-level: first post-war year from Fowler GA line 13 ('Malvern 1868G'); 1875 Guide letters (Fowler 'y'); c.1875 A&G advertisement (RailGa image atgulf1875adv.jpg); end at the 1879 sale (Wikipedia SF&W). Per research/branches/savannah_florida_and_western_railway.txt block [5].
